comments.note: Both RefreshIndexViewModel and MainContentViewModel subscribe to IRefreshOrchestrator.StateChanged but never unsubscribe (no IDisposable). For singleton-lifetime VMs this is harmless today, but if the shell ever reconnects and creates a fresh MainContentViewModel, handlers accumulate on the shared orchestrator. Consider a WeakEventManager or implementing IDisposable.

RefreshIndexViewModel.StartRefreshAsync silently swallows exceptions from IRefreshOrchestrator.StartRefreshAsync (e.g., InvalidOperationException when already running, or unexpected faults). No error surface exists in the VM. A nullable ErrorMessage property and corresponding notification would allow the view to display failure feedback.

AvaloniaFolderPickerService uses IStorageFolder.Path.LocalPath to obtain the local path. IStorageItem.TryGetLocalPath() (Avalonia extension method) is more defensive for non-file URI schemes and should be preferred to avoid silent empty-string returns on edge-case platforms.

MainContentViewModel retains a parameterless constructor solely for backward-compatible test factory lambdas that type-check the VM without exercising its behaviour. Once the project moves to DI-aware test doubles or a factory interface, this ctor can be removed to enforce correct construction at all callsites.

AvaloniaFolderPickerService.PickFolderAsync (src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/AvaloniaFolderPickerService.cs) uses results[0].Path.LocalPath instead of the more defensive results[0].TryGetLocalPath(). On non-file URI schemes this silently returns an empty string rather than null, which would pass the null guard in LibraryFoldersViewModel.AddFolderAsync and persist an empty-string path. Not a blocker for current desktop targets but warrants a follow-up fix. (Originally flagged by Developer pipeline as a low-priority improvement.)

MainContentViewModel.OnRefreshStateChanged fires RefreshCountAsync via fire-and-forget (_ = RefreshCountAsync()). Any exception thrown by IMovieCatalogRepository.GetCountAsync will be silently swallowed. Low risk given the repository is a thin DB call, but a logging fallback would improve observability.

summary: Reviewed 5 files (IFolderPickerService, AvaloniaFolderPickerService, LibraryFoldersViewModel, RefreshIndexViewModel, MainContentViewModel). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low | A04 Insecure Design | src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/AvaloniaFolderPickerService.cs line 37: results[0].Path.LocalPath returns an empty string (not null) for non-file:// URI schemes. The null guard in LibraryFoldersViewModel.AddFolderAsync (line 46) does not catch an empty string, so a non-file URI result would persist an empty-string path to the repository. In practice, IStorageProvider.OpenFolderPickerAsync only returns file:// URIs on all Avalonia desktop targets, so the exploitable surface is negligible. Remediation: replace results[0].Path.LocalPath with results[0].TryGetLocalPath() ?? string.Empty and add an IsNullOrEmpty guard in AddFolderAsync before calling _repository.AddAsync.

Low | A09 Security Logging & Monitoring Failures | src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/RefreshIndexViewModel.cs (StartRefreshAsync) and src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/MainContentViewModel.cs (OnRefreshStateChanged): both fire async work without any exception handling or logging. Orchestrator errors in StartRefreshAsync and repository errors in RefreshCountAsync are silently swallowed, leaving no audit trail for operational failures. Remediation: add try/catch with ILogger logging, or at minimum surface errors to an observable ErrorMessage property so diagnostic information is available.
